title: Calibrate golden baselines and stable CI perf gates for kernel routing and prefill/decode scheduling
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: produce stable, reproducible golden baselines and CI performance gates that capture realistic hybrid workloads (prefill + decode) and kernel selection sensitivity. This ticket covers: (1) defining workload suite variants that exercise attention patterns, kv-cache behaviors, and short/long decode tails; (2) determining statistical baseline methodology (run counts, aggregation, outlier handling); (3) instrumenting the harness to capture kernel routing histograms and percentiles; (4) implementing CI gating logic with flakiness detection and automated quarantine/notification; (5) storing immutable golden artifacts and audit metadata for rollbacks.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Golden baseline artifacts (input seeds, model config, runtime flags) are produced and stored in s3://redwood-bench/gold/runtime-1.22 with checksums.
2) Benchmark harness captures p50/p90/p95/p99 and kernel-selection distributions for each run.
3) CI perf gate script fails PRs that increase p99 by >8% or p95 by >10% relative to rolling baseline, after flakiness checks.
4) Dashboard panels and a runbook exist for triage linking to PRs/trace artifacts.
5) Noise budget parameters and quarantine policy documented in the runbook.
comments: 2026-02-11 - Asha (creator): Scoped initial work. Proposal: start with 3 hybrid workloads: chat-short (prefill 64 tokens + decode 32), long-context completion (prefill 4096 + decode 128), and few-shot retrieval-style prefill (multiple short prefill chunks). Link to spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Golden+Baseline+Spec (internal).

2026-02-18 - Liam (assignee): Prototype harness added to runtime/benchmarks/harness. Initial runs show high variance on p99 when using dynamic kernel selector on A100 (observed ~12% stdev across 7 runs). Experiment PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4321

2026-02-23 - Performance team: Decision: seed workloads deterministically and use 'median-of-5' for golden creation to reduce noise. Also capture raw per-step kernel id histograms to detect selector changes between runs.

2026-02-28 - SRE: CI integration notes — we will run smoke workload in CI on a warmed VM to catch regressions quickly and trigger full bench pipeline asynchronously for more confidence. Implemented a gating script that queries latest rolling baseline from s3 and applies thresholds.

2026-03-03 - Data: Run artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-bench/runs/ENG-15803/2026-03-03-1 (includes kernel_hist.csv, latency_{p50,p95,p99}.csv, perf.trace). Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/benchmarks/runtime-bench

2026-03-06 - Experiment results: Quantized kernel variant reduced decode p99 by 14% on long-context workload but introduced 4% p50 regression for short-chat workload. Trade-off discussion: prefer preserving short-tail latency for interactive customers; will add workload weight to scoring function used by gating logic.

2026-03-08 - Engineering review: Implemented flakiness detector -> marks a run as unstable if p99 stdev across 5 recent runs > 6%. If unstable, CI gate will defer and create a performance investigation ticket instead of failing PRs outright.

2026-03-10 - PRs: Integration PR to common bench infra https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/198, CI gate script PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/ci-scripts/pull/57. Requesting code review from @maria-chen for gating thresholds and @devon-hayes for kernel hist parsing.

2026-03-12 - Next steps (Liam): 1) Finalize scoring function that weights workloads (chat-short 50%, long-context 30%, few-shot 20%). 2) Add golden artifact immutability checks and checksum verification in CI. 3) Draft runbook for triage with example investigations and escalation path. 4) Schedule canary runs on Dedicated pool to validate thresholds under production traffic shapes.
